footer:
Best of Luck,
Cole Slaw
CEO, Aminal Catcher Co.

tiers.bad:
While we appreciate your help for the past 7 days, we'd like to note that our customer satisfaction metric dropped by 80% over the course of your internship. And, to be quite frank, we couldn't be happier to let you go.

Consider yourself lucky that we are a nation of laws, because I'd very much like to deliver you a firm clap on the face.

P.S. We're probably going bankrupt soon, and you will be sued. Our lawyers will get in touch shortly.
tiers.ok:
I'm writing as is tradition when an intern graduates. I honestly don't know much about you, so let's keep it short: if your papers hadn't reached my desk this morning, I wouldn't have known you existed.

Looking at the evals, you did... fine? Anyway, I have more important things to attend to. Thanks for your work, I guess...
tiers.good:
I gotta say, I'm very impressed with your performance. One of the clients you serviced happens to be a good friend of mine, and whenever we hang out he just can't stop talking about your catching skills. And the numbers backed it up.

If you enjoy the work, the offer for a full-time Paid Internship position is on the table. Do think it over.

P.S. The title is mostly formality. We can't actually pay you just yet, since this year's budget is a little tight. Will be a good experience though ;)
tiers.best:
When I was an intern myself, I was told of a prophecy: that once in a thousand years, an intern so gifted at catching aminals the company would never need another intern again, would come knocking on our doors. I didn't believe a word of it. 

And yet here I am, watching the story unfold with my very own eyes. Every request fulfilled. Every species accounted for. You were so good you caught aminals we didn't even know existed.

So the deal is simple: you are hereby promoted to our most sought-after position, Senior Solutions Intern. A leadership track. Cross-functional ownership of synergy initiatives. A role so vital we never found the right fit in over 50 years, is now yours. 

P.S. The position is, as is tradition, unpaid. But the title looks tremendous on a resume, and the experience, I am told, is priceless.
